st_unknown_until_the_id_is: unknown until the ID is known

st_not_joined_automatic_retries_measurem: not joined · automatic retries; measurements/WiFi continue
st_davis_exclusive_mode_see_the: Davis exclusive mode · see the Davis box below
st_none_received_yet_bresser_sensors: none received yet (Bresser sensors send every 12–16 s, IT+ about every 4 s, Fine Offset every 5–80 s, air quality sensors every 10 min)
st_no_device_per_wireless_sensor: no device per wireless sensor — mark your sensors ★ Mine (button next to each sensor, or Settings → Sensors) to get one Home Assistant device per wireless sensor
st_heltec_v4_wireless_build_only: Heltec V4 without PCB: wireless build – PCB inputs disabled (no PCB v2.0 revision ID on GPIO15)
st_forbidden_no_admin_password_configure: Forbidden: no admin password configured (set one via the WiFi portal's "WiFi + MQTT Parameter" section).

st_capture_stopped_download_the_file: Capture stopped - download the file below.
set_9733_mine_numbered_first_in: ★ Mine: numbered first in this order (arrows) – this order is also the priority of the value sources set to Auto, one Home Assistant device each. ○ Received: shown and output everywhere, numbered after yours, no Home Assistant device. ✕ Hidden: never stored, numbered or output (a neighbour's sensor). Changes apply with Save.
set_wi_fi_mdns_hostname_sanitised: Wi-Fi/mDNS hostname (sanitised), MQTT client ID, default topic prefix
set_altitude_for_the_sea_level: Altitude for the sea-level pressure (QNH); latitude / longitude for the sun and moon times (computed on the node) and AWEKAS — they never leave the node otherwise.
set_device_wide_also_affects_mqtt: Device-wide: also affects MQTT, Home Assistant and the LoRaWAN payload.
set_bresser_tfa_lacrosse_it_or: Bresser, TFA / LaCrosse IT+ or Fine Offset / Ecowitt / Froggit sensors (see Wireless sensor type), received with the LoRa chip between uplinks; disables low-power mode
set_auto_listens_to_bresser_it: Auto: listens to Bresser, IT+ 17.241 kbit/s + Fine Offset and IT+ 9.579 kbit/s in turn and stores the type of the first valid packet (from a listed ID, if IDs are set); the status page shows what was found. IT+: e.g. TFA 30.3143/3144/3147/3157/3159.IT (17.241 kbit/s), 30.3155/3156.WD (9.579 kbit/s); with both rates the receiver alternates every 5 s. Fine Offset: Ecowitt / Froggit / Ambient WH65/WS69 7-in-1, WS80, WS85, WS90, WS68, WH31/DP50, WN32/WN32P, WN34, WN35, WH40, WN20, WH51, WH52, WH57, WH55 leak, WH41/WH43/WH45/WH46 air quality (868 MHz versions); same data rate as IT+ 17.241 kbit/s, so both are received together (with IT+ 9.579 kbit/s: 17 s / 5 s alternating). Bresser + another family: the receiver learns each sensor's send interval and switches to its data rate shortly before its next packet (in between 17 s Bresser, 5 s per IT+ data rate, 17 s Fine Offset in turn, to find new sensors); occasional misses when two sensors send at the same moment — still being field-tested
set_on_only_the_sensors_marked: on: only the sensors marked ★ Mine are received (needs at least one); off: all except the hidden ones — the others are numbered after yours
set_hex_comma_separated_max_32: hex, comma-separated, max 32; order = wireless 1–n (1–4 are the value-source choices); each gets a Home Assistant device
set_hex_comma_separated_max_322: hex, comma-separated, max 32; never stored, numbered or output
set_used_for_lorawan_mqtt_weather: used for LoRaWAN, MQTT, weather networks and history; a wireless sensor counts while it sent within 5 min; Auto never takes an indoor sensor (WH45/WH46, WN32P)
set_station_pressure_bme280_or_a: station pressure: BME280 or a wireless sensor with a barometer (Ecowitt WS69 pressure module, WN32P / WH25 — indoor is fine); QNH from the altitude
set_only_wireless_sensors_e_g: only wireless sensors (e.g. Bresser 7-in-1) measure light
set_switching_keeps_the_rain_totals: switching keeps the rain totals continuous (only increases of the selected source count)
set_gust_highest_3_s_mean: gust = highest 3-s mean; other sensors every 10 s or each send
set_davis_anemometer_vane_on_the: Davis anemometer/vane on the PCB; off without a PCB (floating inputs)
set_davis_rain_gauge_on_the: Davis rain gauge on the PCB
set_not_available_on_heltec_v4: not available on a Heltec V4 without PCB v2.0
set_wireless_build_only_pcb_inputs: wireless build – PCB inputs disabled (Heltec V4 without PCB v2.0)
set_keep_rain_statistics_over_a: Keep rain statistics over a power cut
set_saves_rain_sunshine_today_and: saves rain/sunshine today and yesterday, last rain and rain week/month/year to flash at most once per hour, at midnight and before every restart/update, so they survive a power cut; off = kept in RTC RAM only, lost on power loss (and possibly on a firmware update)
set_cal_wizard_hint: 8 or 16 vane positions, recorded with the guided wizard (also in the config portal); saving switches the sensor type to the calibrated table
set_decoder_hint: JavaScript decoder matching this firmware ({0}); paste it into the device profile / payload formatter
set_radio_off_note: Warning: after saving the node is reachable only via the config portal (PRG 3 s) or a LoRaWAN downlink (opens the portal). Only possible while LoRaWAN is enabled and joined.
set_radio_off_not_joined: not joined at the moment — switching off is refused
set_wifi_enabled_hint: off = LoRaWAN-only node: no web interface, MQTT, weather networks or NTP
set_webapi_enabled_hint: off = no web pages and REST API; Wi-Fi, MQTT and uploads keep running
set_radio_off_confirm: I understand: after saving the node is reachable only via the config portal (PRG 3 s) or a LoRaWAN downlink
set_radio_off_refused_confirm: Wi-Fi / web interface off (confirmation not ticked)
set_radio_off_refused_lora: Wi-Fi / web interface off (refused: LoRaWAN is not enabled and joined, the node would be unreachable)
set_heater_max_3_a_and: Heater (max 3 A) and fan (max 1 A) run from the VIN terminal. Auto modes use the BME280 temperature (else DS18B20 #0), thresholds in °C with 1 K hysteresis.
set_v_at_terminal_per_v: V at terminal per V at pin: 1 = direct (ADC useful to ~3.1 V; 3.3 V limit), 1.66667 with R25 15k (0–5 V); older boards: retain their calibration
set_uses_the_aux_pulse_and: uses the AUX PULSE (and AIN) terminals instead of the AUX counter/analog input same calibration as the main anemometer, vane 0–3.3 V from AUX 3V3
set_1_100_10_s_heating: 1–100, 10 s heating cycle (0.1 Hz); auto: power at the full-power temperature
set_rises_linearly_towards_the_full: rises linearly towards the full-power temperature
set_1_100_pwm_tacho_and: 1–100, PWM; tacho and stall check only at 100
set_0_ignore_otherwise_missing_disabled: 0 = ignore; otherwise missing/disabled VE.Direct PV data keeps fan off
set_0_no_limit_otherwise_missing: 0 = no limit; otherwise missing/disabled VE.Direct keeps outputs off (4s LiFePO4: e.g. 12.4)
set_raw_sensor_voltage_is_reported: raw sensor voltage is reported whenever enabled; GPIO3 is never driven as an output
set_terminal_v_per_adc_v: terminal V per ADC V: 1.1 for JP10 1-2 (0-3.3 V), 1.66534 for JP10 2-3 (0-5 V)
set_index_remains_omitted_until_this: index remains omitted until this is enabled and slope/offset are valid
set_experimental_all_fields_apply_at: Experimental. All fields apply at once without a restart; the status page box Davis and the log show the effect. Field-test guide: docs/wireless-sensors.md
set_dip_switch_setting_of_the: DIP switch setting of the ISS / anemometer transmitter (console: Setup → transmitter ID). Other IDs are ignored
set_100_to_100_added_to: -100 to +100; added to every channel. The transmitter's own error moves with temperature; the receiver decodes only within about ±4 kHz
set_0_60_while_searching_try: 0–60; while searching, try the offset in 6-kHz steps around the set one (about 15 s per step)
set_every_4th_packet_is_listened: every 4th packet is listened to 6 kHz above / below to follow a drifting transmitter (costs a few packets)
set_5_500_a_packet_may: 5–500; a packet may arrive this much after the prediction, later = miss
set_5_500_a_packet_may2: 5–500; a packet may arrive this much before the prediction (earlier = another station)
set_narrower_more_sensitive_wider_more: narrower = more sensitive, wider = more frequency tolerance of the filter (not of the demodulator)
set_sniffer_every_packet_to_the: Sniffer: every packet to the log
set_raw_bytes_crc_decoded_values: raw bytes, CRC, decoded values, timing; at most 30 lines per minute in the web log, all of them in /api/davis/log
set_parks_on_the_channel_below: parks on the channel below and logs everything that passes the sync word, also CRC failures — when tracking does not work at all
set_interval_mean_3_s_gust: Interval: mean, 3-s gust and direction since the last uplink. 10 min: the WMO values of the last 10 minutes — do not average those again downstream
set_optional_defaults_to_the_device: optional, defaults to the device name
set_direct_uploads_over_wifi_each: Direct uploads over WiFi, each enabled by filling in its station ID. Enable a network either here or in weather-data-bridge, never both — it would receive every reading twice.
set_only_for_boxes_with_authentication: only for boxes with authentication (default for new boxes)
set_sends_every_value_as_its: Sends every value as its own UDP datagram name=value (e.g. temp=6.6) to a Loxone Miniserver: create a Virtual UDP Input with this port and one command per value, recognition e.g. temp=\v. Names = the keys of /api/data. Values that are currently not valid are not sent; Loxone keeps the last one. Needs WiFi.
set_a_host_name_is_resolved: a host name is resolved without blocking and refreshed every 10 min
set_optional_a_z_a_z: optional, A–Z a–z 0–9 _ . - (max 16), e.g. g75_ to tell several nodes apart on one port
set_0_every_measurement_cycle_else: 0 = every measurement cycle, else 2–3600; wind mean/gust and rain cover the time since the last send
set_light_sleep_between_samples_only: light sleep between samples; only active while Wi-Fi is off
set_pcb_v2_0_off_for: PCB v2.0; off for vanes that need continuous power
set_applies_immediately_slow_data_rates: applies immediately. Slow data rates allow only 51 bytes (SF10–SF12): the node then leaves out the least important values (debug, AUX, outputs, Victron, LiPo, DS18B20, then BME280, rain, wind) until the uplink fits — binary usually fits completely, CayenneLPP often does not. The status page shows what was left out.
set_a_change_is_tested_for: a change is tested for 60 s without restart; if the node cannot connect or neither the gateway nor DNS answers there, it returns to the current network. Another network needs DHCP: switch a static IP off in the same step
set_leave_empty_to_keep_the: leave empty to keep the current one; “remove” = open network
set_for_a_network_that_is: for a network that is not in range yet: stored right away, the node leaves the current network immediately and keeps trying the new one — reach it again via the new network, LoRaWAN (downlink 0x03 opens the config portal) or the button
set_shown_on_the_status_page: shown on the status page and as firmwareUpdate in JSON; installing stays manual (OTA)
set_tags_gitea_or_releases_github: tags (Gitea) or releases (GitHub) API returning names like 2.0.0-beta.3
set_ignored_on_heltec_v4: ignored on a Heltec V4 without PCB v2.0
set_wireless_build_only_pcb_inputs2: wireless build only – PCB inputs disabled
set_adds_diagnostic_fields_to_every: adds diagnostic fields to every payload
set_status_page_wireless_sensors_radio: status page → Wireless sensors → Radio trace
set_records_every_packet_the_receiver: records every packet the receiver gets, for support
set_incomplete_form_submission_nothing_w: Incomplete form submission — nothing was saved.
set_loxone_name_prefix_max_16: Loxone name prefix (max 16 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -)
set_pcb_revision_the_board_identifies: PCB revision (the board identifies itself as v2.0)
set_wifi_network_a_static_ip: WiFi network (a static IP is set for the current network — switch the static IP off in the same step or before, and set it again on the new network)
set_wifi_name_1_32_characters: WiFi (name 1-32 characters, password 8-63 characters or none)
opt_interval_since_the_last_send: Interval (since the last send) – for Grafana etc.
opt_auto_by_flash_size_8: Auto (by flash size: 8 MB = V3, 16 MB = V4)
opt_auto_board_first_then_wireless: Auto (board first, then your ★ sensors in their order)
rft_auto: Auto (search, stores the first type received)
rft_all: All types (keeps listening to every type, nothing is stored)
rft_itplus17_fo: TFA IT+ 17.241 kbit/s + Fine Offset (same data rate, no alternating)
rft_itplus_both_fo: TFA IT+ (both data rates) + Fine Offset
rft_davis: Davis Vantage Pro2 / Vue (exclusive: LoRaWAN paused, no other wireless sensors; experimental)
set_wifi_notest: Saved. The new WiFi network is stored without a test; the node leaves this network now and connects as soon as the new network is in range.
set_wifi_notest_restart: Saved. The new WiFi network is stored without a test; the node leaves this network now, restarts to apply the other network/LoRaWAN settings and connects as soon as the new network is in range.
set_wifi_test: Saved. The node now tries the new WiFi network for up to 60 s. If it connects, it stays there — reach it again by its name or the IP on the display. Otherwise it returns to the current network and this page shows a notice. It reloads in 75 s.
set_wifi_test_restart: Saved. The node now tries the new WiFi network for up to 60 s and then restarts to apply the other network/LoRaWAN settings. If it connects, it stays there — reach it again by its name or the IP on the display. Otherwise it returns to the current network and this page shows a notice. It reloads in 75 s.
set_saved_restarting: Saved. Restarting to apply the new network/LoRaWAN settings — this page reloads in 20 s.
set_intro: live fields apply immediately. restart fields save and restart the node (the in-RAM chart history is lost). Passwords and keys are never displayed — leave empty to keep. Switching WiFi or the web API off and the wind-direction calibration wizard stay in the config portal (hold the button 3 s, or downlink 0x03).
set_language_hint: web pages and setup portal; each browser can still pick its own language in the menu at the top (and on the dashboard)
st_wx_enabled_no_upload: enabled, every {0} s · no upload yet
st_wx_counts: {0} ok / {1} failed since boot · every {2} s
st_dv_acquire: parked on one channel, waiting for the transmitter (up to 15 s per offset step)
st_dv_raw: raw capture, no hopping, values not used
st_left_out: last uplink left out (data rate too slow): {0}
st_uplink_stretched: {0} s (set {1} s, stretched to keep 1 % airtime at this data rate)
st_auto_searching: Auto: searching — Bresser, IT+ 17.241 kbit/s + Fine Offset and IT+ 9.579 kbit/s in turn until the first valid packet
st_auto_searching_mine: Auto: searching — Bresser, IT+ 17.241 kbit/s + Fine Offset and IT+ 9.579 kbit/s in turn until the first valid packet from a sensor marked Mine
st_hidden_in_range: {0} hidden sensor(s) in range (not stored or output; Settings → Sensors)
st_ha_devices: one device per sensor marked ★ Mine ({0}) · topic <prefix>/rf/<ID>
tr_kept: Kept in memory (24 KB) until you discard it, start a new one or restart the node.

tr_on_log_page: Start, download or discard on the log page (admin password).
set_no_sensor_yet: No sensor received yet and none marked ★.
set_only_mine_note: Only my sensors is on: other sensors are not received, so they don't appear here.
set_unhide_note: Set to ○ Received or ★ Mine to unhide.
set_advanced_hint: diagnostics and expert fields: Davis diagnostics, CPU frequency, debug mode, ID lists as text, I/O scale factors, version list URL
set_other_combination: Other combination (bit mask {0}, set by parameter 50)
set_value_sources_note: Wireless sensors appear here as soon as they are received or marked ★ (up to 32), with their name and ID; the number is their place in the table above.
set_interval_hint: 5–3600; stretched automatically if the data rate would exceed 1 % airtime
set_heater_power_at: Heater auto: power at that temperature (%)
set_osem_hint: key=sensorId, comma-separated; keys: temp, hum, press, wind, gust, dir, rain (last hour), rainday, dew, uv, lux — units °C, %, hPa, m/s, °, mm, lx
set_board_hint: detected: {0} ({1} MB flash); V4: without PCB or on PCB v2.0 (its V4 sockets)
set_board_hint_r8: detected: {0} ({1} MB flash) – V4-R8 not supported; V4: without PCB or on PCB v2.0 (its V4 sockets)
log_intro: Rolling view of this device's own serial output (library-internal messages, e.g. from WiFiManager/RadioLib, aren't captured). Auto-refreshes every second.
pt_lorawan_optional_only_for_sending:
LoRaWAN (optional)

Only for sending over a LoRaWAN network (TTN, ChirpStack, ...): switch it on and enter the keys. Not needed for a Wi-Fi station.
pt_low_power_mode_light_sleep: Low-power mode: light sleep between samples (LoRa only, WiFi off; 0=No, 1=Yes)
pt_low_power_mode_switch_the: Low-power mode: switch the wind-vane supply off between readings (PCB v2.0; 0=No, 1=Yes)
pt_appkey_32_hex_chars_leave: AppKey (32 hex chars; leave empty to keep the stored key)
pt_lorawan_region_eu868_us915_au915: LoRaWAN region (EU868, US915, AU915, AS923, IN865, KR920, CN470, RU864)
pt_pcb_revision_12_rev1_2: PCB revision (12=Rev1.2, 13=Rev1.3, 20=v2.0; v2.0 is detected automatically; a Heltec V4 runs on v2.0 only, detected on GPIO15)
pt_altitude_above_sea_level_in: Altitude above sea level in m (0-4000)
pt_wind_sample_interval_in_s: Wind sample interval in s: 1 or 3
pt_lorawan_wind_values_0_interval: LoRaWAN wind values: 0 = interval since the last uplink, 1 = 10-min (WMO)

pt_mqtt_wind_values_0_interval: MQTT wind values: 0 = interval since the last publish, 1 = 10-min (WMO)
pt_wireless_sensors_868_mhz_1: Wireless sensors (868 MHz): 1 = receive with the LoRa chip (between uplinks), 0 = off
pt_wireless_sensor_type_16_auto: Wireless sensor type: 16 = Auto (search: stores the type of the first sensor received), 1 = Bresser, 6 = TFA/LaCrosse IT+ (both rates), 2 = IT+ 17.241 kbit/s only, 4 = IT+ 9.579 kbit/s only, 8 = Fine Offset / Ecowitt / Froggit, 10 = IT+ 17.241 kbit/s + Fine Offset (same data rate), 14 = IT+ both rates + Fine Offset, 7 = Bresser + IT+ / 9 = Bresser + Fine Offset (timed switching between the data rates), 15 = all types (keeps listening, stores nothing), 17 = Davis Vantage Pro2 / Vue (exclusive: LoRaWAN paused, no other sensors; experimental)
pt_wireless_sensors_mine_hex_ids: Wireless sensors 'Mine' (hex IDs, comma-separated, max 32, order = wireless 1-n)
pt_hidden_wireless_sensors_hex_ids: Hidden wireless sensors (hex IDs, never stored or output)
pt_only_my_sensors_1_accept: Only my sensors (1 = accept only the 'Mine' IDs, 0 = all except hidden)
pt_value_sources_temp_hum_wind: Value sources temp/hum, wind, rain, UV, light, pressure (0 auto, 1 board, 2-33 wireless 1-32, 34 off)
pt_wind_direction_offset_in_degrees: Wind direction offset in degrees (-180 to +180)
pt_wind_speed_unit_if_metric: Wind speed unit if Metric (0=km/h, 1=m/s; ignored if Imperial)
pt_wind_direction_sensor_0_potentiometer: Wind direction sensor (0=potentiometer, 1=calibrated table — see 'Calibrate Wind Direction' button)
pt_wind_sensor_on_the_pcb: Wind sensor on the PCB enabled (0=No, 1=Yes; 0 without a PCB)
pt_rain_sensor_on_the_pcb: Rain sensor on the PCB enabled (0=No, 1=Yes; 0 without a PCB)
pt_rain_statistics_today_yesterday_last: Rain statistics (today/yesterday, last rain, week/month/year): save to flash at most hourly and before restarts so they survive a power cut (1=Yes, 0=RTC RAM only)
pt_lorawan_payload_format_1_compact: LoRaWAN payload format: 1 = compact binary (FPort 3, recommended), 0 = CayenneLPP (FPort 1, about twice the size). pt_pcb_v2_0_inputs_outputs2: PCB v2.0 Inputs / Outputs (only used on PCB v2.0)
pt_aux_analog_scale_1_direct: AUX analog scale (1 = direct, 1.66667 with R25 15k for 0-5 V)
pt_2nd_wind_sensor_on_aux: 2nd wind sensor on AUX (0=off, 1=speed at PULSE, 2=speed + direction at AIN)
pt_2nd_wind_vane_offset_in: 2nd wind vane offset in degrees (-180 to 180)
pt_heater_auto_on_below_c: Heater auto: on below °C (off 1 K above)
pt_heater_auto_full_power_at: Heater auto: full power at and below °C
pt_fan_auto_on_from_c: Fan auto: on from °C (off 1 K below)
pt_fan_auto_minimum_pv_w: Fan auto: minimum PV W (0=ignore; missing VE.Direct data=off)
pt_heater_fan_minimum_battery_v: Heater/fan minimum battery V (0=no limit; missing VE.Direct data=off)
pt_uv_sensor_on_gpio3_0: UV sensor on GPIO3 (0=off, 1=on; PCB v2.0 only)
pt_uv_divider_scale_terminal_v: UV divider scale (terminal V per ADC V: 1.1 for JP10 1-2 / 0-3.3 V, 1.66534 for JP10 2-3 / 0-5 V)
pt_uv_index_calibration_slope_index: UV index calibration slope (index per volt, 0.001-30)
pt_board_sensors_and_measurement_pcb: Board sensors and measurement (PCB: Davis wind/rain, BME280 is detected automatically)
pt_wifi_mqtt_parameter_wifi_network:
WiFi + MQTT Parameter

WiFi network credentials and static IP (optional, default DHCP) are configured separately via the "Configure WiFi" menu.

Weather network uploads (AWEKAS, Weather Underground, ...) and time zone are set on the node's web settings page (http://<node-ip>/api/settings) once WiFi is up.
pt_wifi_enabled_0_no_1: WiFi enabled (0=No, 1=Yes) - master switch for MQTT/Web API
pt_device_name_wifi_hostname_mqtt: Device name (WiFi hostname, MQTT client id, default topic prefix)
pt_web_rest_api_settings_page: Web REST API + settings page enabled (0=No, 1=Yes)
pt_admin_password_for_the_web: Admin password for the web settings page and firmware updates (OTA, /update); leave empty to keep
pt_remove_the_stored_admin_password: Remove the stored admin password (settings page locked, OTA unprotected)

pt_mqtt_password_optional_leave_empty: MQTT password (optional; leave empty to keep)
pt_mqtt_topic_prefix_optional_default: MQTT topic prefix (optional, default = device name)
pt_mqtt_security_0_plain_no: MQTT security (0=plain/no TLS, 1=TLS/trust any cert, 2=TLS/verify cert below)
pt_loxone_udp_output_0_no: Loxone UDP output (0=No, 1=Yes): one datagram name=value per value
pt_loxone_miniserver_ip_or_host: Loxone Miniserver IP or host name
pt_loxone_name_prefix_optional_max: Loxone name prefix (optional, max 16 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -)

pt_section_text: A Wi-Fi station with a wireless outdoor sensor only needs the Wi-Fi network ("Configure WiFi"); the fields under Basic setup are optional. After saving, open http://<node-ip>/ (the address is shown on the display) in your network: the setup wizard continues there with the station, location, password and outputs.

set_wifi_chg_stored: Stored the WiFi network “{0}” without a test.
set_wifi_chg_aborted: Could not start the WiFi change to “{0}”: the current network's settings could not be read, so there would be nothing to return to. Nothing was changed.
set_wifi_chg_unreachable: Could not switch to “{0}”: not reachable within 60 s (check the network name and password) — back on the previous network “{1}”.
set_wifi_chg_no_net: Could not switch to “{0}”: connected, but neither the gateway nor DNS answered (wrong network settings or no internet?) — back on the previous network “{1}”.
tr_err_heap: not enough free memory ({0} KiB free, about {1} KiB needed)
wz_intro: Welcome! A few short steps set up the node — each one can be skipped and everything can be changed later under Settings.
wz_open_warning: No admin password is set yet: until you set one (step 5), anyone in your network can change the settings.
wz_station_intro: These are the wireless sensors the node hears right now (the list updates every 10 s). Mark yours with ★ — they get fixed numbers and one Home Assistant device each — and hide neighbours’ sensors with ✕.
wz_searching: Searching for your station… The node tries Bresser, Ecowitt / Froggit and TFA / LaCrosse in turn; most stations appear within a minute.
wz_waiting: No sensor received yet — they send every few seconds to a minute.
wz_location_intro: Where is the station? The altitude matters most: the sea-level pressure (QNH) is calculated from it.
wz_name_hint: a name for the station, e.g. Garden — also its network name (<name>.local) and MQTT ID
wz_altitude_hint: metres above sea level at the station (map apps or the municipality website show it); needed for the correct sea-level pressure
wz_geo_fail: Position not available — please enter it by hand.
wz_units_intro: How should values be shown — here, in Home Assistant, on MQTT and in the LoRaWAN payload?
wz_pw_intro: Strongly recommended: protect the settings with a password. The browser then asks for it (user name admin); it also protects firmware updates.
wz_pw_set: A password is set. Enter a new one only to change it.
wz_outputs_intro: Optional: where should the measurements go? Open a section to fill it in; leave the rest for later.
wz_restart_note: Some settings (station name, MQTT …) take effect after a restart: Finish restarts the node once.
wz_later_hint: closes the wizard; you can start it again any time under Settings → System.
wz_restarting: Done. The node restarts to apply the new settings — this page reloads in 25 s.
wz_run_hint: language, wireless station, location, units, password and outputs step by step
set_cal_temp_hint: -10 to 10, added to the selected temperature source (board or wireless)
set_cal_press_hint: -20 to 20, added to the station pressure before the sea-level (QNH) reduction
set_cal_factor_hint: 0.5 to 2, 1 = unchanged; applies to the selected source (board or wireless)
set_cal_rf_hint: ID:temperature:humidity[:rain:wind:UV:light[:wn20]], comma separated — offsets in K and %, then factors 0.5–2 (1 = unchanged), e.g. 1A2B3C4D:-0.4:+3 or 20001234:0:0:0.908 (WN20: rain factor after the Ecowitt wiki; :wn20 = experimental rate-dependent correction). Corrects that sensor everywhere (status, rfSensors, MQTT, value sources); the rain factor applies to the increments, not to the counter shown. Up to 32 sensors. Presets: :wn20 or :wh40 (×1.016); WH51 soil moisture: :ad=AD0-AD100 (raw AD in dry soil and in water).
set_rec_reset_hint: Takes effect at once after a confirmation and cannot be undone; the minimum / maximum values or the charts start again.
set_reset_confirm: Really delete? This cannot be undone.
set_hist_reset: Delete chart history (24 h and 7 days)
set_rain_reset: Reset rain statistics (today to this year, since start)
set_astro_needs_loc: Sunrise, sunset and moon times need the latitude and longitude.
set_sun_method_hint: radiation (WMO-like): needs a W/m² sensor (Davis solar radiation) as the light source and the location; otherwise the illuminance threshold is used
set_bk_hint: A JSON file with all settings of this page. Restoring checks every value like Save does, lists what changed and restarts if needed; the LoRaWAN session is kept.
set_bk_secrets_warn: The file then contains the WiFi, admin, MQTT and weather-network passwords and the LoRaWAN AppKey in plain text — keep it private.
set_bk_invalid: Not a settings backup of this node type — nothing was changed.
set_bk_newer: The backup is from a newer firmware (format {0}) — update the firmware first. Nothing was changed.
set_bk_nochange: Restored — the backup matches the current settings.
al_rules_note: Up to 12 rules. Thresholds in the units of the unit setting. A value that is not available (sensor silent, no source) never raises or clears an alarm. Value “– (free)” deletes a rule.
al_sensor_id_hint: hex ID of a wireless sensor (status page), for “Wireless sensor value”
al_clear_hint: the alarm ends at this value (hysteresis); for warnings and yes/no values use 0.5 for both
al_msg_hint: empty = default text; placeholders {name} {value} {unit} {threshold} {sensor} {time} and all of the custom upload, e.g. {temp}
al_tpl_hint: goes into the first free slot when saving; adjust it afterwards
al_channels_note: Tokens and keys are write-only. Sent one at a time by the upload task; the result is on the status page.
al_mqtt_hint: events to <prefix>/alarm for rules with the MQTT channel; the states (<prefix>/alarm/<n>, Home Assistant) are always published
al_wh_url_hint: placeholders allowed (URL-encoded), e.g. {name}, {value}; treated like a password in the settings backup
al_test: Save this tab and send a test
al_test_queued: Alarm settings saved, test notification queued — the result appears on the status page under Alarms within a minute.
cu_note: Any HTTP service: a URL template (and for POST a body) with placeholders such as {temp}, {wind:kmh}, {qnh:inhg}, {temp:.1} — see Help → Weather networks. Wind is the 10-minute WMO wind.
cu_url_hint: URL template, empty = off; treated like a password in the settings backup
set_wow_hint: wow.metoffice.gov.uk, the number in brackets on the site page; WOW announced its closure
set_cwop_hint: e.g. CW1234 (wxqa.com); needs latitude / longitude; sent to cwop.aprs.net:14580
set_cwop_pass_hint: -1 for CWOP IDs (CW…, DW…, EW…); licensed radio amateurs: their passcode
set_disp_note: The PRG button switches the display on; while it is on, a short press shows the next screen. Default as before: the status screen for 20 s.
set_disp_night_hint: local time, 0–23; both equal = never off (with “always”); PRG still switches it on for 20 s
set_dv_rain_filter_hint: implausible jumps of the tip counter are held until the next counter packet confirms them; rejected jumps go to the log and the radio trace
set_dv_rain_pkt: Rain: tips per packet without confirmation
set_dv_rain_pkt_hint: 1–127; default 8 (1.6 mm with 0.2-mm cups, about every 10 s)
set_dv_rain_min_hint: 1–127; a confirmed jump above this rate is a counter reset, not rain; default 50 (10 mm/min)
set_names_as_text_hint: ID:name, separated by |, e.g. 900181A2:Hochbeet|3000C201:Cellar; up to 24 characters each
c_busy_retry: The node is busy with an encrypted upload and low on memory - please try again in a few seconds.
wz_found_confirm: is this your station? If not, search again or choose the type under Settings → Sensors.
set_ota_hint: Upload universal-weather-node-<version>.bin – or, from 2.0.0-rc.1 on, the -factory.bin (only its firmware part is written). Other files are refused before anything is written; settings, rain totals and records are kept. The node restarts afterwards. Behind a reverse proxy, allow uploads of at least 2.5 MB.
ota_need_password: Firmware upload over the web interface needs an admin password – set one (Settings → System) or use the config portal.
ota_restart_in: This page opens the status page in {0} s.
ota_lost: Connection lost – if the node is restarting, reload the page in a minute.
ota_reconnect: The node restarts with the new firmware (about 20 s) and keeps its address. This page then opens the status page – check the firmware version there. If it does not come back, reload the page.
